summary:
**Orbital Architect** is an interactive space mission design simulator developed using Godot 4 and GDScript. It transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, hands-on learning experience.

The project allows users to act as NASA Flight Directors and Systems Engineers, designing spacecraft, selecting components, and managing real-world mission scenarios inspired by NASA missions. Using verified NASA open engineering data, the simulator applies physics-based calculations to validate spacecraft designs, evaluating parameters such as mass, propulsion, orbital velocity, power consumption, eclipse endurance, and radiation constraints. Players can then launch their spacecraft, monitor live telemetry, perform orbital maneuvers, and manage mission operations.

Orbital Architect addresses the gap between unrealistic commercial space games and complicated professional aerospace software by combining scientific accuracy with interactive gameplay. Its bilingual English-Arabic interface, lightweight design, browser compatibility, and free accessibility make aerospace education available to more students.

The project is important because it makes advanced space engineering easier to understand, encourages critical thinking and problem-solving, and inspires the next generation of aerospace engineers and scientists.
details:
Project Details – Orbital Architect

Orbital Architect is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform that allows users to experience the challenges faced by real aerospace engineers and NASA Flight Directors.

How It Works

Users begin by selecting one of five mission scenarios inspired by real NASA missions or entering the Sandbox Lab to create their own missions. They then design a spacecraft by selecting its launch vehicle, orbital destination, structural bus, power systems, batteries, propulsion, avionics, communication systems, and scientific payloads.

A real-time physics validation engine evaluates their designs using aerospace principles, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, orbital velocity models, and eclipse duration calculations. Once the spacecraft passes validation, users can launch it, monitor telemetry, perform station-keeping maneuvers, capture scientific targets, and manage onboard data storage.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes aerospace engineering more accessible by combining scientific concepts with practical experimentation. It develops problem-solving, systems thinking, and engineering decision-making skills. Its bilingual English-Arabic interface, lightweight architecture, and browser compatibility help overcome language, hardware, and financial barriers to STEM education.

Our intended impact is to inspire students worldwide to explore aerospace engineering and understand the complexity of real space missions through interactive learning.

Tools and Technologies

  • Godot 4: Main game engine.
  • GDScript: Core programming language.
  • Procedural Vector Graphics: Lightweight visual elements.
  • NASA Open Data: Scientific and engineering reference data.
  • SHA-256: Local account password hashing.
  • Physics Models: Rocket equation, orbital mechanics, and eclipse calculations.

Creativity and Innovation

Orbital Architect creatively combines the accessibility of educational games with the technical depth of aerospace engineering software. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, it makes players experience engineering trade-offs and understand how changing one spacecraft parameter can affect the entire mission.

Factors Considered

Our team prioritized scientific accuracy, educational value, accessibility, bilingual support, performance on standard hardware, realistic mission scenarios, and an intuitive user experience. We also considered different skill levels through progressive difficulty tiers, allowing beginners to learn while challenging more advanced users.
